newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CHARLEVILLE ON FULL ALERT
The south-west Queensland town of Charleville is on full flood alert with reports of a mass of brown water moving south towards the Murray Darling River system.
Already houses are inundated or threatened in the towns of Charleville, Augathella, Tambo, and Bollon and dozens of rural properties are isolated.
Shire mayor, Graham Andrews says the northern part of Charleville may have to be evacuated because about 60 centimetres of water could rush through the town.
Emergency service workers are organising drops of food tents and stretchers with major roads, highways and rail links blocked throughout the southern inland.
A catering corp will be flown into Charleville today to provide up to 3000 meals for emergency workers, and residents sheltering in a local school.
BEAZLEY URGES INTEREST RATE CUT
Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley is urging the Reserve Bank board to cut official interest rates again at its monthly meeting today.
Observers are divided about the prospects of another rate cut, following the two reductions late last year.
Mr Beazley, says businesses especially need lower interest rates, and a further cut would not jeopardise inflation.
PEOPLE'S CONVENTION A LUXURY, SAYS LIBERAL MP
Federal Liberal MP Wilson Tuckey says a people's convention on a republic would be a misuse of money in the current economic climate.
The Prime Minister, John Howard, is expected to outline Cabinet's proposals for a convention on constitutional change to a meeting of federal Coalition MPs.
But Mr Tuckey says spending $50-million on changing the name of the Governor General from His Excellency to Mr President will not put a meal on anyone's table.
The federal Coalition are holding their first meeting of the year, with a republic emerging as one of the key talking points.
The Government is also set to honour its promise to allow for half of the convention's delegates to be popularly elected.
NEW CODE FOR NSW POLICE
New South Wales police officers face dismissal if they breach a new code of conduct launched today by Police Commissioner Peter Ryan.
Under the code, police must never commit a corrupt or unethical act, and must avoid financial and other conflicts of interest.

They're also required to comply with the rights of the public, and are banned from soliciting or accepting gifts or benefits, using offensive language, drinking alcohol on the job and misbehaving in private.
There'll be an amnesty on minor offences for police officers not under investigation by the Royal Commission.
And Commissioner Ryan says he hopes for one of the biggest cultural changes for the service - the encouragement of whistleblowers.
WORKING PARTY ON CHRONIC FATIGUE
Federal Liberal backbencher, Brendan Nelson, wants more clinicians with experience in chronic fatigue syndrome on a working party looking into the disorder.
The working party has been set up the Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, in consultation with the Royal Australasian College of Physicians
It'll establish national guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome.
But Doctor Nelson says doctors and relatives of people with the illness are concerned that only five of the 15 member committee have direct experience and knowledge of it.
The concern has been echoed by researchers at Newcastle University whose studies confirmed the debilitating disorder is not all in the patient's mind.
Dr Hugh Dunstan says the University has developed a web-page on the internet with links to the latest research from around the world.
POLICE INVESTIGATING SENATOR'S EXPENSES
The Australian Federal Police has confirmed its investigating allegations relating to the use by Liberal Senator Bob Woods of parliamentary expenses.
Senator Woods last night announced he was resigning from the Senate because of personal reasons.
A Federal Police spokesman says officers have been interviewing several people during the investigation, but can't confirm the nature of the allegations involving Senator Woods.
Senator Woods, the Parliamentary Secretary for Health, has been in politics for nearly ten years.
